meanings: to play (a keyed or plucked instrument)

components.note: 弓 (bow) — a bowstring springing back
单 (dān) gives a loose sound hint for tán

example.fact: 弹 is read tán for plucking, bouncing or flicking: 弹钢琴, 弹吉他, 弹性 (elasticity). Read dàn, it means bullet or shell: 子弹, 炸弹, so the two readings are worth keeping apart.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — tents and curtains are made of cloth
长 (zhǎng) gives the sound — they differ only in tone

example.english: A mosquito net hangs over the bed.
example.fact: 帐 is a cloth canopy: 帐篷 (tent), 蚊帐 (mosquito net). Money and accounts are now normally written 账 (结账, 账号), and mixing up 帐 and 账 is a common error.

components.note: 广 (a building) — the upper-left cover
又 (hand) — measuring by hand is the root idea

example.english: The temperature today is thirty degrees.
example.fact: 度 is a degree of temperature or angle (三十度), and also a unit of electricity in everyday use (一度电). It means to spend time in 度假 (take a vacation), and shows up in 温度 (temperature), 速度 (speed) and 过度 (excessive).

components.note: 北 (north) — originally two people back to back
⺼ (flesh) — a body part

example.fact: 背 has two readings: bèi (back, behind; to recite from memory, as in 背单词) and bēi (to carry on the back: 背书包). 背景 is background, and 背后 means behind or behind someone's back.

components.note: Simplified form of 節, whose original picture was a bamboo joint; the meaning broadened to section and holiday

example.hanzi: 春节是中国最重要的节日。
example.pinyin: Chūn Jié shì Zhōngguó zuì zhòngyào de jiérì.
example.english: Spring Festival is China's most important holiday.
example.fact: 节 grew from the segment of a bamboo stem to mean a festival (节日), a section, and a measure word for class periods and train carriages: 一节课, 一节车厢. 节约 means to economise.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — arranging things with the hands
非 (fēi) gives a loose sound hint for pái

example.fact: 排 is a row (第一排, the first row; 一排座位) and the action of arranging: 排队 (queue), 排名 (ranking), 排除 (rule out). 排骨 is spare ribs and 排球 is volleyball.

components.note: 犭 (animal) — a pig is a domestic animal
者 (zhě) gives a loose sound hint for zhū

example.pinyin: Tā jiā yǎng le hěn duō zhū.
example.fact: 猪 is the pig, the last animal of the zodiac. Unqualified 肉 means 猪肉 (pork) in China, and 小猪佩奇 is the Chinese name of the cartoon Peppa Pig.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — following behind someone
阝 is the remnant of 隋 (suí), the old phonetic part of the traditional form 隨

example.fact: 随 is to follow or go along with: 随着 (along with), 随时 (at any time), 随身 (carried on one's person) and 随手 (without extra effort, as in 随手关门, "close the door as you go"). 随便 means "as you like" and is one of the most-used words in casual conversation.

components.note: A picture of a cow's head with two horns

example.fact: 牛 counts with 头 (一头牛). In slang 牛 means impressive: 你真牛！ ("you're awesome"). It forms 牛肉 (beef) and 牛奶 (milk).

components.note: 瓦 (pottery tile) — bottles were once ceramic
并 (bìng) gives a loose sound hint for píng

example.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le yì píng shuǐ.
example.english: I bought a bottle of water.
example.fact: 瓶 is both a bottle and the measure word for bottled things: 一瓶水, 一瓶啤酒. 瓶子 is a bottle, 花瓶 a vase, and 瓶颈 ("bottle neck") means a bottleneck, as in English.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — breathing and sucking in through the mouth
及 (jí) gives a loose sound hint for xī

example.pinyin: Qǐng shēnshēn de xī yì kǒu qì.
example.fact: 吸 is to take in: 吸烟 (smoke), 吸引 (attract), 吸收 (absorb), 吸尘器 (vacuum cleaner). 呼吸 (breathe) pairs 呼 (exhale) and 吸 (inhale).

components.note: 女 (woman) — the woman is the one who marries into a family
家 (jiā) gives the sound — they differ only in tone

example.pinyin: Tā jià gěi le yí gè yīshēng.
example.fact: 嫁 is used for a woman marrying (嫁给), and 娶 (qǔ) for a man marrying. 嫁人 is the plain "get married" for women, and 嫁祸于人 means to shift the blame onto someone else.

components.note: In the oldest script it was a simple cross shape; the number sense is a borrowed use of that form

example.english: I get up at seven every day.
example.fact: 七 appears in 七夕 (the seventh day of the seventh lunar month, a Chinese Valentine's Day) and the idiom 七上八下 ("seven up eight down"), describing an anxious, unsettled heart.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — vegetables are leafy plants
采 (cǎi) gives the sound — they differ only in tone

example.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de cài hěn hǎochī.
example.english: The food at this restaurant is delicious.
example.fact: 菜 means both "vegetables" and "a dish": 点菜 (order dishes), 菜单 (menu), 中国菜 (Chinese food). In slang 菜 means unskilled: 我太菜了 ("I'm so bad at this"), especially in gaming.

components.note: 攵 (tap, action) — an action radical, to correct by effort
己 (jǐ) gives a loose sound hint for gǎi

example.english: I want to change the plan a bit.
example.fact: 改 is to change something into something better or different: 改正 (correct), 改革 (reform), 改变 (change). 改天 ("another day") is a polite way of postponing, as in 改天再聊.

components.note: 心 (heart) — intentions and thoughts
音 (yīn) gives the sound — they differ only in final

example.fact: 意 is the heart-level idea behind words. It appears in 意思 (meaning), 注意 (pay attention), 同意 (agree), 愿意 (be willing), 生意 (business). 不好意思 means "sorry" or "embarrassed", and 有意思 means interesting.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — earning money
兼 (jiān) gives only a loose sound hint for zhuàn

example.pinyin: Tā yí gè yuè zhuàn duōshao qián?
example.english: How much does he earn a month?
example.fact: 赚 stresses profit and gain, as in 赚钱 (make money), and its counterpart is 赔 (péi, to lose money): 赚了还是赔了? 挣钱 (zhèngqián) is another common way to say earn, closer to earning through effort.

components.note: Two wings or feathers pointing in opposite directions — opposition, and so "not"

example.fact: 非 is a formal "not" and a prefix "non-": 非法 (illegal). 非 … 不可 means "must" (literally "not doing X is not acceptable"). 非常 ("very") is literally "not ordinary", and 非洲 is Africa.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a spoken word or sound
吾 (wú) gives the sound — an exact match

example.fact: 唔 is the Cantonese negative "not" (m4), written with a mouth radical to mark it as a spoken-dialect word. Standard Mandarin writing uses 不 instead, so you will mostly meet 唔 in Hong Kong texts and comics.

excludeSuggestion: Cantonese-only written form (m4, "not"); not used in standard Mandarin.

components.note: 二 (two strokes) above — in the old picture, a mark above the head
儿 (a person with legs) — a figure whose head is marked, hence "head, first"

example.fact: 元 is the formal word for the yuan, found on banknotes, while speech uses 块 (kuài): 二十块. It also means first or origin: 元旦 (New Year's Day), 元首 (head of state), and 元宵 is the Lantern Festival.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread) — weaving and braiding thread
扁 (biǎn) gives the sound — they differ only in tone

example.english: She knows how to knit sweaters.
example.fact: 编 is to weave or braid (编辫子), and by extension to compile or compose: 编辑 (editor), 编程 (to program), 编号 (serial number). 编故事 can mean to invent a story, and 你别瞎编 means "stop making things up".

components.note: 戈 (a spear-like weapon) — fighting
占 (zhàn) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Liǎng guó zhījiān fāshēng le zhànzhēng.
example.english: A war broke out between the two countries.
example.fact: 战 is bound to compounds: 战争 (war), 战斗 (fight), 战士 (soldier), 挑战 (challenge), 战胜 (defeat), 冷战 (Cold War). It also works in sports and games as "match", as in 战队.

components.note: An ancient picture whose original meaning is uncertain; later borrowed for "second" and for the sound of "Asia"

example.fact: 亚 is short for 亚洲 (Asia), taken from the sound of "Asia". It also means "second" or "sub-": 亚军 (runner-up) and 亚热带 (subtropics). It appears in transliterations, such as 亚马逊 (Amazon).

components.note: 又 (hand) replaced the complicated left part of the traditional 戲
戈 (weapon) — stage fighting and mock combat

example.fact: 戏 is a play or a performance, counted with 场. 看戏 means to watch a play, and 戏剧 is drama. 游戏 is a game, and 戏精 is internet slang for an overly dramatic person.

components.note: 爪 (claw) — crawling and clawing along
巴 (bā) gives the sound — they differ only in initial and tone

example.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi zài dìbǎn shang pá.
example.english: The little child is crawling on the floor.
example.fact: 爬 is to crawl or climb, as in 爬山 (hike), 爬楼梯 (climb the stairs). In tech it appears in 网络爬虫 (web crawler), literally "crawling bug". 登 (dēng) is the more formal "climb".

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — money staked in gambling
者 (zhě) gives a loose sound hint for dǔ

example.fact: 赌 is to gamble or bet: 赌钱, 赌博 (gambling, formal), 赌场 (casino), 打赌 (to make a bet). 赌气 ("gamble breath") is a different idea: to act out of spite or sulk.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — spitting with the mouth
土 (tǔ) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Bié zài dì shang tǔ tán.
example.fact: 吐 is read tǔ for spitting or letting something out (吐出来), and tù for vomiting (呕吐, 吐了). The internet word 吐槽 (tǔcáo) means to roast or complain humorously about something.

components.note: 酉 (wine jar) — blending and mixing drinks
己 (jǐ) gives only a loose sound hint for pèi

example.hanzi: 这条裙子配这双鞋很好看。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo qúnzi pèi zhè shuāng xié hěn hǎokàn.
example.english: This skirt looks nice with these shoes.
example.fact: 配 means to match, complement or dispense: 配合 (cooperate), 配套 (matching set), 配菜 (side dish), 配眼镜 (get glasses made). It also means to be worthy of: 他不配 ("he doesn't deserve it").

components.note: 讠 (speech) — language is spoken words
吾 (wú) gives only a loose sound hint for yǔ

example.pinyin: Nǐ huì shuō jǐ zhǒng yǔyán?
example.english: How many languages can you speak?
example.fact: 语 forms the names of languages: 汉语, 英语, 日语. It also appears in 语言 (language), 语法 (grammar), 成语 (idiom) and 自言自语 (to talk to oneself). In messaging, 语音 means a voice message.

components.note: Simplified form of 絲, which showed two skeins of silk thread side by side

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu shì sī zuò de.
example.english: This garment is made of silk.
example.fact: 丝 is silk thread and anything thread-like: 铁丝 (wire), 土豆丝 (shredded potato, a classic dish), 一丝笑容 (a trace of a smile). 丝绸之路 is the Silk Road, and 粉丝 means "fans", a pun on the English word with the noodle word.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person staying as before
乃 (nǎi) gives only a loose sound hint for réng

example.pinyin: Tā réngrán zhù zài lǎo fángzi lǐ.
example.english: He still lives in the old house.
example.fact: 仍 is a formal adverb for "still": 仍然, 仍旧. In everyday speech people more naturally say 还 or 还是. You will meet 仍 more in writing, news and reports than in casual talk.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — lodging or staying under a roof
奇 (qí) gives the sound — they differ only in initial and tone

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng jì yì fēng xìn.
example.english: I want to mail a letter.
example.fact: 寄 is to send by post or courier: 寄信, 寄快递, 邮寄. It also means to lodge or entrust: 寄宿 (board at school), 寄托 (to pin hopes on). 寄 is for mailing, whereas 送 is to deliver or give by hand.

components.note: 口 (mouth, a vessel opening) appears four times
犬 (dog) sits in the middle, traditionally read as a dog guarding a set of vessels

example.fact: 器 is a bound word for devices and containers: 机器 (machine), 武器 (weapon), 乐器 (musical instrument), 电器 (appliance), 器官 (organ). The idiom 大器晚成 means a great talent matures late.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — talking and listening
卯 (mǎo) gives a loose sound hint for liáo

example.fact: 聊 is casual chatting, usually reduplicated or as 聊天 (to chat, including text chat). 无聊 means bored or boring: the older sense of 聊 was "to depend on", so it is something with nothing to hold on to.

components.note: 女 (woman) — a mother or young woman
良 (liáng) gives the sound — they differ only in initial

example.english: She's going back to her parents' home to visit them.
example.fact: 娘 is a colloquial "mother" (爹娘 mom and dad). It appears in 娘家 (a married woman's parental home), 新娘 (bride) and 姑娘 (girl, young woman, read gūniang).

components.note: 犭 (animal) — a wild animal
王 (wáng) gives the sound — they differ only in initial

example.english: They are partying wildly in the street.
example.fact: 狂 means wild or mad and also arrogant: 疯狂 (crazy), 狂欢 (revel; 狂欢节 is a carnival), 狂妄 (arrogant), 狂风 (gale).

components.note: 扌 (hand) — dragging with the hand
也 (yě) gives only a loose sound hint for tuō

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhuōzi tuō dào le ménkǒu.
example.english: He dragged the table to the door.
example.fact: 拖 is to drag or tow: 拖地 (mop the floor), 拖鞋 (slippers, "dragged shoes"), 拖拉机 (tractor, "dragging machine"). It also means to put things off: 拖延 (procrastinate).

components.note: 口 (mouth) — blowing with the mouth
欠 (an open-mouthed figure) — a radical for mouth actions

example.pinyin: Fēng bǎ mén chuī kāi le.
example.english: The wind blew the door open.
example.fact: 吹 is to blow: 吹风机 (hair dryer), 吹气球 (blow up a balloon) and 吹笛子 (play a flute). 吹牛 ("blow a cow") means to brag, and in slang 吹了 can mean a relationship or deal fell through.

components.note: The parts (宀 over 丰 and 口) do not clearly show "harm"; the character is learned as a whole

example.fact: 害 is to harm: 伤害 (injure), 害虫 (pest), 有害 (harmful). It also has feeling words: 害怕 (afraid), 害羞 (shy). In online slang a drawn-out 害 conveys a sigh of resignation.

components.note: 攸 (yōu) gives the sound — a near match for xiū
彡 (decorative strokes) — adorning, trimming and improving

example.hanzi: 我的电脑坏了，要找人修。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de diànnǎo huài le, yào zhǎo rén xiū.
example.english: My computer is broken and needs someone to fix it.
example.fact: 修 is to repair or improve: 修理 (repair), 修改 (revise), 修路 (repair roads), 装修 (renovate a home). It also means study or self-cultivation: 进修 (further study), 修养 (accomplishment), 修炼 (cultivate oneself).

components.note: 心 (heart) — anxiety is felt in the heart
刍 (chú) gives only a loose sound hint for jí

example.fact: 急 is anxious or urgent: 着急 (to worry, be impatient), 急事 (urgent matter), 急诊 (emergency room). Say 他急了 to mean "he got flustered or lost patience".

components.note: Simplified shape: 几 sheltering 乂; the traditional 風 held a 虫 inside

example.fact: 风 is wind and, extended, custom or style: 风俗 (customs), 风景 (scenery), 作风 (style of conduct). 风水 ("wind and water") is the practice of feng shui, and 台风 is a typhoon.

components.note: 而 is the upper part of the character
女 (woman) is the lower part; the parts do not clearly explain the meaning

example.fact: 耍 is to play or fool around, and to play a trick: 耍赖 (act shamelessly), 耍帅 (show off), 耍心眼 (scheme). In Sichuan dialect 耍 is the everyday word for "hang out" or "play".

components.note: 罒 (net) — an old gauze or net
夕 replaces the complicated lower part of the traditional 羅

example.fact: 罗 is mostly seen in transliterated names (罗马 Rome) and as the surname Luo. In words it appears in 罗盘 (compass), 罗列 (list out) and 张罗 (to take care of arrangements).

excludeSuggestion: Mostly a transliteration syllable (罗马) and a surname rather than a standalone word.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person bowing the head
氐 (dǐ) gives the sound — they differ only in tone

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shēngyīn fàng dī yìdiǎn.
example.english: Please keep your voice down a little.
example.fact: 低 is the opposite of 高 and also a verb: 低头 (lower the head, or yield). 低声 is a low voice, 低价 low price, 低碳 low-carbon, and 低头族 is slang for "heads-down" phone addicts.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — what is left after cutting
乘 (chéng) gives the sound — they share the same final

example.pinyin: Pánzi lǐ hái shèng yí kuài dàngāo.
example.english: There is one slice of cake left on the plate.
example.fact: 剩 is to be left over: 剩下 (be left), 剩饭 (leftover rice), 剩菜 (leftovers). 剩女 ("leftover women") is a contested term for unmarried women past their late twenties, often considered derogatory.

components.note: 饣 (food) — a meal
反 (fǎn) gives the sound — they differ only in tone

example.fact: 饭 is both cooked rice and a meal: 米饭 (rice), 早饭 (breakfast), 吃饭 (eat a meal). 吃饭了吗？ ("Have you eaten?") is a common greeting in China. 饭店 means restaurant or hotel.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — the brain is body tissue
凶 (xiōng) is the remnant of the old phonetic part; its sound match is weak

example.pinyin: Tā hěn cōngming, nǎozi zhuàn de kuài.
example.fact: 脑 is the brain: 脑子 (brain, mind), 大脑 (cerebrum), 头脑 (mind) and 脑袋 (head, colloquial). 电脑 ("electric brain") is the everyday word for a computer.

components.note: 火 (fire) — heat and agitation
页 (head) — traditionally read as a feverish, troubled head

example.fact: 烦 is annoyed or annoying: 烦人 (irritating), 烦恼 (worries), 麻烦 (trouble). 麻烦你 + verb ("sorry to trouble you to…") is a very polite way to ask a favour: 麻烦你帮我拿一下.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — tone and melody are about sound
周 (zhōu) gives only a loose sound hint for diào

example.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē de diàozi hěn hǎotīng.
example.english: The tune of this song is very pleasant.
example.fact: 调 has two readings: diào (tune, tone, transfer, investigate: 声调, 调查, 调动) and tiáo (adjust, mix: 调整, 空调, 调皮). 空调 (air conditioner) is read kōngtiáo, so check the reading in each word.
